name: Liberia — citizenship by birth or naturalisation restricted to persons who are Negroes or of Negro descent
origin_test: Race. The applicant must be a Negro or of Negro descent; the test qualifies BOTH citizenship by birth and citizenship by naturalisation, and no other person can hold either.
instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Liberia, 1986
quote_original: In order to preserve, foster and maintain the positive Liberian culture, values and character, only persons who are Negroes or of Negro descent shall qualify by birth or by naturalization to be citizens of Liberia.
basis: Constitution of the Republic of Liberia (1986), Chapter IV (Citizenship), Article 27(b)
notes: This is a racial qualification on the face of the Constitution and it is recorded here as written. It is a GATE, not a grant: art. 27(b) does not confer citizenship on anyone, it disqualifies everyone who is not a Negro or of Negro descent from acquiring it by either route. The actual grants sit in art. 27(a) (continuity of existing citizens), art. 28 (one Liberian parent) and the naturalisation provisions of the Aliens and Nationality Law, Title 4 of the Liberian Code of Laws Revised, which the Legislature is directed by art. 27(c) to frame 'adhering to the above standard'. No degree of descent is stated, which is why neither unlimited nor a maximum_degree is asserted. Source is the Ministry of National Defence's published PDF of the 1986 Constitution, which carries a text layer; the Judiciary's copy at https://judiciary.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/CONSTITUTION-OF-THE-REPUBLIC-OF-LIBERIA.pdf is a 19 MB scan with NO text layer and cannot be quote-gated, and legislature.gov.lr does not resolve from this network (NXDOMAIN on both apex and www). ON THE 2022 DUAL CITIZENSHIP ACT: the 2022 amendment to the Aliens and Nationality Law (widely reported as removing the automatic loss of Liberian citizenship on naturalising elsewhere, and equalising maternal transmission) is an ordinary Act of the Legislature and therefore cannot and did not touch art. 27(b) — art. 91 of the same Constitution requires that any amendment be 'ratified by two-thirds of the registered voters, voting in a referendum conducted by the Elections Commission not sooner than one year after the action of the Legislature'. No referendum removing art. 27(b) has been carried, and the clause is present in the consolidated text published on mod.gov.lr and quoted above, so it remains in force. The 2022 Act's own text could not be verified against a Liberian government host: the copy circulating at liblaw.org is a scan with no text layer, and the Law Library of Congress note at loc.gov returns 403 to non-browser clients, so no quote from the 2022 Act is recorded here.

name: Sierra Leone — citizenship confined to persons of negro African descent
origin_test: Race and descent. 'Person of negro African descent' is a defined term: under the 1973 Act as enacted, a person whose father and father's father are or were negroes of African origin; the qualification runs through the citizenship-by-birth and registration limbs of the Act.
instrument: The Sierra Leone Citizenship Act, 1973 (Act No. 4 of 1973)
articles: s.1(1), definition of 'person of negro African descent'
quote_original: "person of negro African descent" means a person whose father and father's father are or were negroes of African origin;
basis: Sierra Leone Citizenship Act 1973, Part I (Preliminary), section 1(1), definition of 'person of negro African descent'
notes: SOURCE CAVEAT, read this before citing. The Parliament of Sierra Leone site (parliament.gov.sl) times out on every request from this network, and SierraLII (sierralii.gov.sl, the Judiciary's Laws.Africa instance) does not hold the 1973 Act at all — its legislation collection starts in the 2010s and a full-text search for 'negro' across it returns one 1968 judgment and no statute. The document cited here is published by the MINISTRY OF INTERNAL AFFAIRS of Sierra Leone, the department responsible for citizenship, in its own 'Legislations/Acts' list at https://www.moia.gov.sl/documents — but the PDF is a print-to-PDF of the Refworld reproduction and carries UNHCR branding on its first page. It is therefore official by publisher and NOT official by provenance, and should be replaced with a Government Printing Department gazette scan when one becomes reachable. AMENDED TEXT: the definition quoted is the 1973 text as enacted. It was replaced by section 2 of the Sierra Leone Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2006 (Act No. 11 of 2006, Supplement to the Sierra Leone Gazette Vol. CXXXVII No. 60 of 28 December 2006), which substitutes: 'person of negro African descent' means a person whose mother or father and any of the grand parents of the mother or father is or was a Negro of African descent. That widens the line to either parent and any grandparent — still parent plus grandparent, still a racial test — and it is why relations and maximum_degree are recorded as parent+grandparent rather than the narrower paternal-only 1973 line. The only copy of the 2006 gazette supplement located is www.sierra-leone.org/Laws/2006-11.pdf, a privately run mirror (The Sierra Leone Web), which is NOT an official source and is named here only to say where the amended wording was read.

name: Ghana — right of abode for a person of African descent in the Diaspora
origin_test: African descent, as a continental/racial category, with no ancestor identified and no link to any Ghanaian citizen required. Granted on application, in the Minister's discretion and with the President's approval.
quote_original: (b) a person of African descent in the Diaspora.
basis: Immigration Act 2000 (Act 573), Part II, section 17(1)(b) (Right of Abode)
notes: THIS IS NOT CITIZENSHIP AND MUST NOT BE MODELLED AS ONE. Section 17 confers a residence status. Section 17(1) opens: 'Subject to this section the Minister may on an application and with the approval of the President grant the status of right of abode to any of the following persons:' and lists (a) a Ghanaian by birth, adoption, registration or naturalisation who lost Ghanaian citizenship by acquiring a foreign nationality, and (b) the diaspora limb quoted. The Ghana Immigration Service, which administers it, describes the content of the status on its own page (https://gis.gov.gh/service/right-of-abode/, verbatim: 'Right of Abode is a form of residence status conferred on a person who meets the following criteria; a Ghanaian by birth, adoption, registration or naturalization within the meaning of the Citizenship Act who by reason of his acquisition of a foreign nationality has lost his Ghanaian citizenship; and a person of African descent in the Diaspora.') — the rights are to reside permanently, enter without a visa, and work without a work permit. Section 18 governs the consequences of the status and section 19 lets the High Court revoke it. Nothing in ss.17-19 attaches any citizenship consequence or naturalisation discount to the status — citizenship is governed separately by the Citizenship Act 2000 (Act 591), which was not read for this row and should be checked before any claim is made about a shortened naturalisation clock. Discretionary presidential grants of citizenship to diaspora Africans around the 2019 'Year of Return' are a separate, non-entitlement phenomenon and are deliberately not recorded as a route. No ancestor is specified in s.17(1)(b) and no generational limit is stated, so neither unlimited nor a maximum_degree is asserted. Source is the Parliament of Ghana's own institutional repository copy of Act 573, which has a text layer; note that repository.parliament.gh sits behind a bot filter that intermittently 403s bare requests.

name: Ethiopia — identification card for a foreign national of Ethiopian origin (the 'yellow card')
origin_test: Ethiopian origin traced up to three generations: the person must either have held Ethiopian nationality before acquiring a foreign one, or have had at least one parent, grandparent or great-grandparent who was an Ethiopian national. Persons who forfeited Ethiopian nationality and acquired Eritrean nationality are excluded by name.
instrument: Providing Foreign Nationals of Ethiopian Origin with Certain Rights to be Exercised in their Country of Origin Proclamation No. 270/2002 (Federal Negarit Gazeta, 8th Year No. 17, 5 February 2002)
quote_original: 1) "Foreign National of Ethiopian Origin" means a
basis: Proclamation No. 270/2002, Part One, Article 2(1), definition of 'Foreign National of Ethiopian Origin'
notes: NOT CITIZENSHIP. The card confers residence-and-work rights on a foreign national, and art. 6 keeps back exactly the things that mark citizenship: the holder 'Shall have no right to vote or be elected to any office at any level of Government' and shall not be employed in the National Defence, Security or Foreign Affairs. Art. 5 gives the rights that make it valuable: no entry visa or residence permit needed to live in Ethiopia; the right to be employed without a work permit; no exclusion from the pension scheme; the right to be treated as a domestic investor under the investment law; and disapplication of the Civil Code arts. 390-393 restrictions on foreigners. WHY THE QUOTE IS A FRAGMENT: justice.gov.et (Federal Ministry of Justice) publishes the actual Federal Negarit Gazeta pages as scanned PDFs with an OCR text layer, and the Gazeta prints Amharic and English in two parallel columns, so `pdftotext -layout` interleaves them and the longest contiguous English run is one printed line. The line quoted is clean; the continuation lines are OCR-degraded ('foeign !1ational', 'great grand pare~ts') and would not be an honest verbatim quote. The full art. 2(1) reads, in the printed English: 'Foreign National of Ethiopian Origin' means a foreign national, other than a person who forfeited Ethiopian nationality and acquired Eritrean nationality, who had been Ethiopian national before acquiring a foreign nationality; or at least one of his parents or grand parents or great grand parents was an Ethiopian national. The three-generation ceiling is stated on the face of the provision, hence maximum_degree 3 and unlimited false. Implementing instrument: Council of Ministers Regulation No. 101/2004 (Federal Negarit Gazeta No. 34, 21 March 2004), at https://justice.gov.et/en/?jet_download=b9039a648486253998736ccad9f22fe63e3cee35, whose art. 3(1) states verbatim (verified): 'Ethiopian Origin shall be issued with Identification' — the card is issued by the Authority for Security, Immigration and Refugee Affairs if the applicant is in Ethiopia, or through an Ethiopian Mission if abroad. The Federal Supreme Court's Digital Law Library also lists Proclamation 270/2002 but puts the document behind a login, so it is a metadata-only portal for this text and was not used.

name: Rwanda — Rwandan nationality by origin, on application, for persons of Rwandan origin and their descendants
origin_test: Rwandan origin, defined recursively as a parental link to Rwanda through having one parent who is himself or herself of Rwandan origin. The applicant must have been born to at least one parent who is Rwandan by ancestry rather than by acquisition, and must produce testimony, a relative holding Rwandan nationality by origin, or any other proof of Rwandan origin.
instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda of 2003 revised in 2015 (consolidated 2023)
quote_original: (5) All persons of Rwandan origin and their
basis: Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda of 2003 revised in 2015, Article 25(5) (Right to a homeland and nationality)
notes: The full provision reads: '(5) All persons of Rwandan origin and their descendants are, upon request, entitled to Rwandan nationality.' WHY THE QUOTE IS A FRAGMENT: the Official Gazette prints the Constitution in three parallel columns — Kinyarwanda, English, French — and `pdftotext -layout` interleaves them line by line, so the longest contiguous English run is one printed line. Every published copy checked has this property (Rwanda Law Reform Commission consolidation 2023, judiciary.gov.rw, migeprof.gov.rw copy of the 2015 revision); no single-language official edition was found. OPERATIVE IMPLEMENTATION: Organic Law nº 002/2021.OL of 16/07/2021 relating to Rwandan nationality, published by the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration at https://www.migration.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/pdf_files/og_special_of_28.07.2021_ubwenegihugu_nyarwanda.pdf. Art. 3(2°) defines the test (verified fragment: '2º Rwandan origin: a relationship' — full text: 'Rwandan origin: a relationship linking a person to Rwanda as a result of having one parent of Rwandan origin'). Art. 5 (verified fragment: 'nationality by origin is a person of Rwandan') states that a person eligible to apply for Rwandan nationality by origin is a person of Rwandan origin as provided for by the Organic Law. Art. 6 sets the conditions: to be born to at least one Rwandan parent who is a Rwandan not through acquisition but by virtue of Rwandan ancestry, and to provide at least one of (a) testimony by the applicant or by at least one person corroborated by evidence, (b) a relative who has Rwandan nationality by origin, (c) any other proof demonstrating his or her Rwandan origin. Art. 40 adds a parallel recovery-of-nationality-by-origin procedure. THE 1959-1994 PROVISION ASKED ABOUT NO LONGER EXISTS. It was art. 7 of the 2003 Constitution as originally adopted (Rwandans and their descendants deprived of nationality between 1 November 1959 and 31 December 1994 reacquiring it on returning to settle). Neither string '1959' nor '1994' appears anywhere in the 2015-revised Constitution as consolidated in 2023, nor anywhere in Organic Law nº 002/2021. The dated clause has been superseded by the undated, generation-unbounded origin route recorded here, which is broader. Because the definition is recursive and closes no generational list, neither unlimited nor a maximum_degree is asserted. Rwanda's existing atlas row (rwanda-citizenship-at-birth-by-parent) is the ordinary one-parent descent rule and is a different thing from this.

name: Nigeria — citizenship by birth for persons born before independence with a parent or grandparent belonging to a community indigenous to Nigeria
origin_test: Membership of an indigenous community. Either a parent or any grandparent must belong or have belonged to a community indigenous to Nigeria; a proviso additionally requires that a parent or grandparent was born in Nigeria.
instrument: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended)
quote_original: every person born in Nigeria before the date of independence, either of whose parents or any of whose grandparents belongs or belonged to a community indigenous to Nigeria;
basis: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, Chapter III (Citizenship), section 25(1)(a)
notes: This is the ethnic-origin limb of Nigerian citizenship and it is genuinely an origin test — 'a community indigenous to Nigeria', not descent from a citizen. It is however SPENT as an acquisition route: it applies only to persons born in Nigeria before the date of independence, which s.25(2) defines as 'the 1st day of October 1960', so the youngest possible beneficiary was born in September 1960. Its live effect is derivative: s.25(1)(b) makes a person born in Nigeria after independence a citizen by birth if either parent or any grandparent is a citizen of Nigeria, and s.27 deems a parent or grandparent to have been a citizen if they would have had that status by birth had they been alive on the date of independence — so the indigenous-community test still determines whose descendants qualify today. The proviso limits it: 'Provided that a person shall not become a citizen of Nigeria by virtue of this section if neither of his parents nor any of his grandparents was born in Nigeria.' A PREVIOUS RUN FAILED ON A SCANNED PDF; this one does not. The copy cited is published by the National Human Rights Commission (nigeriarights.gov.ng), a Nigerian federal statutory body, and has a clean text layer. Two other .gov.ng copies were tested and rejected: nigeriarights.gov.ng/files/constitution.pdf has a text layer whose left margin is clipped ('ery person born in Nigeria...', 'enous to Nigeria') so verbatim quotes fail, and edojudiciary.gov.ng returns 406 to non-browser clients. nass.gov.ng does not resolve, and nassnig.org — which looks like the National Assembly — is now a squatted commercial law-marketing domain and must not be cited.

name: Nigeria — citizenship by registration for a person of full age born outside Nigeria with a Nigerian grandparent
origin_test: None. This is a descent test, not an origin test: it turns on a grandparent's citizenship, not on ethnicity or membership of a group.
instrument: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended)
quote_original: every person of full age and capacity born outside Nigeria any of whose grandparents is a citizen of Nigeria.
basis: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, Chapter III (Citizenship), section 26(2)(b), read with section 26(1)
notes: Recorded because it is the grandparent limb the brief asked for, and because it is routinely confused with the origin limb in s.25(1)(a). It is registration, not citizenship by birth, and it is discretionary: s.26(1) provides that such a person 'may be registered as a citizen of Nigeria, if the President is satisfied that' he is of good character, has shown a clear intention of his desire to be domiciled in Nigeria, and has taken the Oath of Allegiance in the Seventh Schedule. 'May' plus presidential satisfaction plus a domicile intention is not an entitlement. The ceiling of two degrees is on the face of the provision — grandparent, no further. Registration is also subject to s.28, which restricts dual citizenship for citizens other than by birth. The sibling limb, s.26(2)(a), is 'any woman who is or has been married to a citizen of Nigeria' and is gender-asymmetric; it is noted here because a reader scanning s.26 will meet it first.

name: Algeria
origin_test: Algerian nationality claimed as nationality of origin may be proved by filiation from two ascendants in the paternal or maternal line who were born in Algeria and enjoyed Muslim personal status there.
instrument: Ordonnance n° 70-86 du 15 décembre 1970 portant code de la nationalité algérienne, art. 32, as modified and completed by ordonnance n° 05-01 du 18 Moharram 1426 correspondant au 27 février 2005, art. 7
quote_original: ligne paternelle ou maternelle, nés en Algérie et y ayant
quote_translation: paternal or maternal line, born in Algeria and having there enjoyed [Muslim status]
basis: Ordonnance n° 70-86 du 15 décembre 1970 (code de la nationalité algérienne), art. 32 as amended by ordonnance n° 05-01 du 27 février 2005, art. 7 — Journal officiel de la République algérienne n° 15 du 27 février 2005, p. 16
notes: The Journal officiel PDF is set in two columns, so pdftotext -layout interleaves the facing column into every extracted line; only line-length fragments can be verified character-for-character. Four fragments of the same provision each verified MATCH=True against this URL: '« Art. 32. — Lorsque la nationalité algérienne est'; 'prouvée par la filiation découlant de deux ascendants en'; 'ligne paternelle ou maternelle, nés en Algérie et y ayant'; 'joui du statut musulman.'. Read in column order the provision is: « Art. 32. — Lorsque la nationalité algérienne est revendiquée à titre de nationalité d'origine, elle peut être prouvée par la filiation découlant de deux ascendants en ligne paternelle ou maternelle, nés en Algérie et y ayant joui du statut musulman. » This is an evidentiary rule for proving nationality of origin, not a separate application route: it conditions proof of Algerian nationality of origin on descent from two ascendants who held Muslim personal status in colonial Algeria, i.e. a religious/national-origin qualification distinct from ordinary descent from a citizen parent (art. 6, as amended 2005: 'Est considéré comme Algérien l'enfant né de père algérien ou de mère algérienne'). The 2005 amendment widened the line from paternal only to paternal or maternal. Degree of the ascendants is not specified in the text and no generational cutoff is stated, so unlimited is recorded as null rather than true. Naturalisation (arts. 10-11) and acquisition by marriage (art. 9 bis, inserted 2005) were checked in the same instrument and contain no ethnic or national-origin limb.

name: Egypt
instrument: Law No. 26 of 1975 concerning Egyptian Nationality (قانون رقم 26 لسنة 1975 بشأن الجنسية المصرية), arts. 3 and 4
basis: Law No. 26 of 1975 on Egyptian Nationality, arts. 3 and 4 — record located in the Egyptian judiciary's official legislation database (Court of Cassation, cc.gov.eg), promulgation date 29/05/1975, published in the Official Gazette issue 22
notes: No verified quote: the only official Egyptian host that carries the instrument returns metadata only. The record at https://cc.gov.eg/legislation/860127042 (title 'قانون رقم 26 لسنة 1975 بشأن الجنسية المصرية', نوع التشريع قانون, منشور فى الجريدة الرسمية — العدد ۲۲, تاريخ النشر ۱۹۷٥/۰٥/۲۹) states 'النص الكامل متاح للمشتركين' — full text is subscriber-only. Other Egyptian government hosts probed in this pass: egypt.gov.eg, emigration.gov.eg and alwakaea.gov.eg do not resolve; sis.gov.eg and moj.gov.eg and parliament.gov.eg resolve but no full text of Law 26/1975 was located on them. The art. 4 limb described in the brief (privileged naturalisation for a person who 'belongs by racial origin to a country the majority of whose population is Arabic-speaking or whose religion is Islam') therefore remains UNVERIFIED here and must not be recorded as fact in either direction. Non-official aggregators that do carry the text are excluded by the source rules.

name: Morocco
instrument: Dahir n° 1-58-250 du 6 septembre 1958 portant code de la nationalité marocaine, as amended by loi n° 62-06 (dahir n° 1-07-80), art. 9
basis: Secrétariat Général du Gouvernement (sgg.gov.ma) consolidated-texts register — the official Moroccan publisher of the Bulletin Officiel and of consolidated statutes

Its consolidated-texts register at /arabe/textesconsolides.aspx was enumerated in full and contains no entry for the code de la nationalité / مدونة الجنسية (it covers e.g. loi 36.21 on civil status but not nationality). Legacy Bulletin Officiel archive paths of the form /BO/bo_fr/2007/BO_5514_fr.pdf (the BO carrying loi 62-06) return 404; the live BO paths follow a different scheme (/BO/AR/3111/{year}/...) for which no pre-2010 archive index was reachable. adala.justice.gov.ma and justice.gov.ma do not resolve. name: Tunisia
instrument: Code de la nationalité tunisienne (décret du 26 janvier 1956), arts. 12, 20-24, 39
basis: Imprimerie Officielle de la République Tunisienne (iort.gov.tn), publisher of the Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne

name: Eritrea
instrument: Eritrean Nationality Proclamation No. 21/1992, art. 2 ('person of Eritrean origin' — resident in Eritrea in 1933)
basis: Ministry of Information of the State of Eritrea (shabait.com) — the only Eritrean government host reachable in this pass
notes: No verified quote and no official Eritrean legal-publication host. Eritrea maintains no online Gazette of Eritrean Laws; shabait.com (Ministry of Information) resolves but is a news portal carrying no text of Proclamation No. 21/1992, and eritrea.be (embassy) does not resolve. The 1933-residence 'person of Eritrean origin' test in art. 2 is therefore UNVERIFIED here. Every text of Proclamation 21/1992 that could be located sits on excluded aggregators, so this row records the absence of a reachable official source rather than any conclusion about the law's content.

name: Somalia
instrument: Somali Citizenship Law No. 28 of 22 December 1962, art. 2; Provisional Constitution of the Federal Republic of Somalia (2012), art. 8; any post-2016 replacement citizenship law
basis: Ministry of Justice of the Federal Republic of Somalia (moj.gov.so); Immigration and Citizenship Agency (immigration.gov.so)
notes: No verified quote. Somali federal hosts do resolve — moj.gov.so, moi.gov.so, parliament.gov.so, villasomalia.gov.so and immigration.gov.so all returned 200 — but none publishes a legislative text repository. moj.gov.so exposes no law or gazette section; immigration.gov.so, the agency that administers citizenship, publishes only news items (link inventory enumerated: every 'citizenship' hit is a press release, none a statute). No text of Law No. 28 of 22 December 1962, of art. 8 of the 2012 Provisional Constitution, or of any 2016+ replacement citizenship law was reachable on an official Somali host. The 'of Somali origin' / Somali-race limb of art. 2 is accordingly UNVERIFIED; absence of a reachable source, not a finding on the law.

name: Cabo Verde
instrument: Lei n.º 80/III/90 (Lei da Nacionalidade) as amended, including Lei n.º 64/IV/92, Lei n.º 41/VIII/2013 and the 2024 amending law
